title: Effective theories: proof search and decision procedures

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel’s Theorems
based_on.pages: 33–35 (§§4.3–4.5, Theorems 4.1–4.2); 304–306 (§40.5, Theorems 40.6–40.7); corrected second-edition reprint, August 2020

summary: Enumerate formal consequences, turn completeness into a terminating proof search, and decide equality and dense-order sentences by explicit quantifier elimination.
abstract: A program can search for a proof by checking proposed finite derivations, provided the axioms can themselves be listed by a program. Every provable sentence will eventually be found, but an unsuccessful search may run forever. For a consistent theory that proves or refutes every sentence, searching for a proof of the sentence and its negation together gives a terminating decision procedure. We also construct direct algorithms for infinite sets with equality alone and for dense linear orders without endpoints. They remove quantifiers by finite manipulations of formulas, reducing each sentence to a Boolean calculation. These examples connect general proof search with the more specific information that makes a theory decidable.
